questions.stem: Structural isomers are compounds that have:
options: the same structural formula but different molecular formulas
the same atoms bonded in the same order but arranged differently in space
different molecular formulas but the same functional group
the same molecular formula but atoms bonded in a different order
questions.explanation: Structural isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are connected, such as butane and 2-methylpropane. Stereoisomers have the same connections but a different arrangement in space.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers does the non-cyclic alkane C₆H₁₄ have?
questions.explanation: They are hexane, 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane. Drawing the same chain bent or numbered from the other end does not create a new isomer.

questions.stem: Which alkene can exist as cis and trans isomers?
options: But-2-ene
But-1-ene
Propene
2-methylpropene
questions.explanation: Geometrical isomerism needs restricted rotation about C=C and two different groups on each carbon of the double bond. In but-2-ene each double-bond carbon carries H and CH₃. The others each have at least one double-bond carbon carrying two identical groups (two H atoms or two CH₃ groups).

questions.stem: Including geometrical isomers, how many non-cyclic alkenes have the formula C₄H₈?
questions.explanation: The alkenes are but-1-ene, cis-but-2-ene, trans-but-2-ene and 2-methylpropene. Counting but-2-ene only once gives 3, which misses the geometrical isomers.

questions.stem: cis-1,2-dichloroethene has a higher boiling point than trans-1,2-dichloroethene. Why?
options: The cis isomer has a larger molar mass, so it has stronger dispersion forces
The cis isomer forms hydrogen bonds, but the trans isomer cannot form any
The cis isomer has stronger covalent bonds, which must break when it boils
The cis isomer is polar, so it has dipole-dipole forces in addition to dispersion forces
questions.explanation: In the cis isomer both C-Cl dipoles point to the same side, giving a polar molecule; in the trans isomer they cancel. The isomers have identical molar masses, and boiling breaks intermolecular forces, not covalent bonds.

questions.stem: A chiral carbon atom is a carbon atom that:
options: is bonded to four different atoms or groups
is bonded to two identical groups and a double bond
is part of a carbon-carbon double bond
is bonded to three hydrogen atoms
questions.explanation: A carbon with four different groups has two mirror-image arrangements that cannot be superimposed, giving optical isomers. A carbon in a double bond has only three groups attached.

questions.stem: Which compound contains a chiral carbon atom?
options: Butan-1-ol
2-methylpropan-2-ol
Butan-2-ol
Propan-2-ol
questions.explanation: In butan-2-ol, carbon 2 is bonded to H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅, four different groups. In propan-2-ol, carbon 2 carries two CH₃ groups, so it is not chiral.

questions.stem: Which alkane has a chiral carbon atom?
options: 3-methylhexane
3-methylpentane
2-methylpentane
2,2-dimethylbutane
questions.explanation: Carbon 3 of 3-methylhexane is bonded to H, CH₃, C₂H₅ and C₃H₇, four different groups. In 3-methylpentane carbon 3 has two ethyl groups, and in 2-methylpentane carbon 2 has two methyl groups, so neither is chiral.

questions.stem: A pair of optical isomers (enantiomers):
options: differ only in the position of a double bond along the carbon chain
are non-superimposable mirror images that rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions
are superimposable mirror images that rotate plane-polarised light in the same direction
have different molecular formulas but the same melting and boiling points
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are mirror images that cannot be superimposed. They have the same melting point, boiling point and molar mass, but rotate plane-polarised light equally in opposite directions, and they can act differently in the body.

questions.stem: Which amino acid has no chiral carbon atom?
options: Cysteine, whose side chain is CH₂SH
Glycine, whose side chain is H
Alanine, whose side chain is CH₃
Serine, whose side chain is CH₂OH
questions.explanation: In a 2-amino acid, the central carbon carries H, NH₂, COOH and the side chain R. When R is H, as in glycine, two groups are identical, so the carbon is not chiral. All the other common amino acids have a chiral central carbon.

questions.stem: Markovnikov's rule states that when HX adds to an unsymmetrical alkene, the hydrogen atom adds to the carbon of the double bond that:
options: already has more hydrogen atoms attached
already has fewer hydrogen atoms attached
is closer to the end of the chain numbered 1
is attached to the larger alkyl group
questions.explanation: The hydrogen goes to the double-bond carbon that already carries more hydrogen atoms, and X goes to the more substituted carbon. This predicts the major product.

questions.stem: What is the major product when hydrogen bromide adds to propene?
options: 2-bromopropane
1-bromopropane
1,2-dibromopropane
propan-2-ol
questions.explanation: By Markovnikov's rule, H adds to carbon 1 (CH₂, which has more H atoms) and Br to carbon 2, giving 2-bromopropane as the major product. 1,2-dibromopropane would form from Br₂, not HBr.

questions.stem: Propene reacts with steam in the presence of an acid catalyst. What is the major product?
options: Propanal
Propanoic acid
Propan-2-ol
Propan-1-ol
questions.explanation: Water adds across the double bond as H and OH. By Markovnikov's rule, H goes to the CH₂ carbon and OH to the middle carbon, giving propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. Propanal and propanoic acid would need oxidation.

questions.stem: Which alkene gives only one structural isomer when it reacts with hydrogen chloride, so that Markovnikov's rule is not needed?
options: Hex-1-ene
2-methylpropene
Propene
Hex-3-ene
questions.explanation: Hex-3-ene is symmetrical about its double bond, so adding H and Cl either way round gives 3-chlorohexane. The other alkenes are unsymmetrical and can form two products, of which Markovnikov's rule predicts the major one.

questions.stem: What is the major product when 2-methylpropene reacts with hydrogen chloride?
options: 1-chloro-2-methylpropane
2-chlorobutane
1-chlorobutane
2-chloro-2-methylpropane
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds to the CH₂ carbon, which has more H atoms, and Cl to the carbon carrying the two methyl groups, giving the tertiary haloalkane 2-chloro-2-methylpropane. Butane-based names are wrong because the carbon skeleton is branched.

questions.stem: Compared with LDPE, HDPE has:
options: more branching, so its chains pack more closely
less branching, so its chains pack less closely
cross-links between chains, so it cannot melt
less branching, so its chains pack more closely
questions.explanation: HDPE chains have very few branches, so they pack closely in ordered regions. LDPE has many branches that keep its chains apart, giving a lower density.

questions.stem: Why is HDPE stronger and more rigid than LDPE?
options: Its chains are joined by covalent cross-links that LDPE lacks
Its chains contain polar groups that form hydrogen bonds
Its monomer contains more carbon atoms than the LDPE monomer
Its closely packed chains have stronger dispersion forces between them
questions.explanation: Both are made from ethene, but the unbranched HDPE chains pack closely, so there are more contacts and stronger dispersion forces between chains. LDPE's branches prevent close packing, making it softer, more flexible and less dense. Neither has hydrogen bonding.

questions.stem: Two polyethene samples are tested. Sample A: density 0.96 g/cm³, softens at about 130 °C. Sample B: density 0.92 g/cm³, softens at about 110 °C. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: A is HDPE, because its unbranched chains pack closely
A is LDPE, because its branched chains pack closely
B is HDPE, because its chains have more branches
B is HDPE, because its chains are cross-linked
questions.explanation: Closely packed, unbranched chains give HDPE a higher density and stronger dispersion forces between chains, so more energy is needed to soften it. Branches in LDPE keep its chains apart, lowering both density and softening temperature.

questions.stem: In isotactic polypropene, the methyl groups are:
options: on alternating sides of the chain
randomly arranged along the chain
joined to methyl groups on other chains
all on the same side of the chain
questions.explanation: Isotactic means all the methyl groups are on one side, syndiotactic means they alternate regularly, and atactic means they are randomly arranged.

questions.stem: Why is atactic polypropene soft and rubbery, while isotactic polypropene is hard and strong?
options: Random methyl groups stop the chains packing closely, so the polymer is amorphous
Random methyl groups form cross-links, so the chains cannot slide past each other
Atactic chains are much shorter, because their monomer is a different alkene
Isotactic chains contain double bonds that make the polymer more rigid
questions.explanation: Regularly placed methyl groups (isotactic or syndiotactic) let chains pack in ordered, crystalline regions with stronger dispersion forces between them. In the atactic form the random arrangement prevents ordered packing. All forms come from the same monomer, propene.

questions.stem: Polytetrafluoroethene (PTFE) is used to coat non-stick frying pans. Which feature of its structure explains its chemical inertness and low friction?
options: Weak C-C bonds that break easily, so food cannot attach
Polar C-F bonds that form hydrogen bonds with water in food
Many C=C double bonds that remain in the polymer chain
Strong C-F bonds, with fluorine atoms surrounding the carbon chain
questions.explanation: The C-F bond is very strong, and the fluorine atoms form a sheath around the carbon backbone, so few substances react with or stick to PTFE. Its monomer is tetrafluoroethene, CF₂=CF₂; like other addition polymers, the chain has no double bonds left.

questions.stem: Polylactic acid (PLA) is described as biodegradable, while polyethene is not. Why?
options: PLA contains no oxygen atoms, so it oxidises much more easily than polyethene does
PLA contains ester links that can be hydrolysed, but polyethene has only C-C and C-H bonds
PLA is an addition polymer, and addition polymers are broken down easily by microbes
PLA chains are much longer than polyethene chains, so microbes digest them more quickly
questions.explanation: PLA is a condensation polymer of lactic acid with ester links in its backbone, which water and microbes can hydrolyse. Polyethene is an addition polymer with a backbone of strong, non-polar C-C bonds that microbes break down only very slowly.

questions.stem: Nylon-6,6 fibres are very strong. Which feature of its structure contributes most to this?
options: Dispersion forces only, because the chains are non-polar
Ionic bonds between charged ends of neighbouring chains
Hydrogen bonds between amide groups on neighbouring chains
Covalent cross-links between ester groups on neighbouring chains
questions.explanation: Nylon is a polyamide. The N-H and C=O groups of amide links on neighbouring chains form hydrogen bonds, which hold the chains strongly together. Polyesters contain ester links, which cannot form hydrogen bonds with each other.

questions.stem: Polyesters such as PET and polyamides such as nylon are both:
options: addition polymers
made from a single alkene monomer
polymers with no oxygen atoms in the chain
condensation polymers
questions.explanation: Both form when monomers with two functional groups join and release a small molecule, usually water, at each link. Addition polymers such as polyethene form from alkene monomers with no by-product.

questions.stem: In a 2-amino acid, the amino group and the carboxyl group are:
options: at opposite ends of a long carbon chain
both attached to the side chain R
joined to each other by a peptide bond
both attached to the same carbon atom
questions.explanation: A 2-amino acid has the general structure H₂N-CH(R)-COOH: the amino and carboxyl groups are both on carbon 2, counting the carboxyl carbon as carbon 1. The side chain R is also attached to that carbon.

questions.stem: Amino acids are crystalline solids with high melting points and dissolve well in water. Why?
options: They contain only dispersion forces, which are strong in large molecules
They exist as zwitterions, with strong ionic attractions between them
They are non-polar, so they pack closely in a crystal lattice
They form covalent network lattices, like diamond, in the solid state
questions.explanation: The basic amino group accepts a proton from the acidic carboxyl group, forming a zwitterion, ⁺H₃N-CH(R)-COO⁻. The attractions between these charged ends are strong, like ionic bonds, giving high melting points, and the charges interact well with water.

questions.stem: In which form does glycine mainly exist in a strongly acidic solution?
options: H₂N-CH₂-COOH
⁺H₃N-CH₂-COOH
H₂N-CH₂-COO⁻
⁺H₃N-CH₂-COO⁻
questions.explanation: At low pH there is a high concentration of H⁺, so the carboxylate group is protonated and the amino group stays protonated, giving a positive ion. In strongly basic solution the anion H₂N-CH₂-COO⁻ forms instead.

questions.stem: The isoelectric point of an amino acid is the pH at which:
options: it is fully deprotonated and carries a negative charge
it moves fastest towards the positive electrode
it has no overall charge, so it does not move in an electric field
it is fully protonated and carries a positive charge
questions.explanation: At the isoelectric point the amino acid exists mainly as the zwitterion, which has an overall charge of zero, so it does not migrate during electrophoresis. Below this pH it is positive; above it, negative.

questions.stem: Glycine (pI 6.0), lysine (pI 9.7) and glutamic acid (pI 3.2) undergo electrophoresis in a buffer at pH 6.0. Which result is expected?
options: Lysine moves to the positive electrode, glutamic acid to the negative, glycine stays
All three move to the positive electrode, because the buffer is slightly acidic
Glycine moves the furthest, because it is the smallest of the three
Lysine moves to the negative electrode, glutamic acid to the positive, glycine stays
questions.explanation: At a pH below its pI an amino acid is protonated and positive, so lysine moves to the negative electrode. Above its pI it is negative, so glutamic acid moves to the positive electrode. Glycine is at its pI, has no net charge and stays at the origin.

questions.stem: In a paper chromatogram, an amino acid spot travels 3.6 cm and the solvent front travels 9.0 cm from the origin. What is the Rf value?
questions.explanation: Rf = distance moved by the amino acid / distance moved by the solvent = 3.6 / 9.0 = 0.40. An Rf value is always less than 1; 2.5 comes from inverting the ratio.

questions.stem: In paper chromatography with a polar stationary phase, amino acid P has Rf 0.70 and amino acid Q has Rf 0.25. Which statement is correct?
options: Q moved further because it is more soluble in the mobile phase than P is
Q has the higher Rf, because it spends more time in the stationary phase
P is more soluble in the mobile phase and less attracted to the stationary phase than Q
P is more strongly attracted to the stationary phase and less soluble in the mobile phase
questions.explanation: A substance with a high Rf spends more of its time dissolved in the moving solvent and less adsorbed on the stationary phase, so it travels further. Q is more strongly attracted to the polar stationary phase, so it moves less.

questions.stem: How can an unknown amino acid be identified by paper chromatography?
options: Measure how far it travels, because each moves a fixed distance in any solvent
Run it alone, because Rf values do not depend on the solvent used
Compare its Rf with those of known amino acids run in the same solvent and conditions
Compare its spot colour with a chart, because each amino acid has its own colour
questions.explanation: Rf values depend on the solvent and stationary phase, so the unknown is compared with standards run on the same paper under the same conditions. Most amino acids are colourless and are shown with a locating agent, such as ninhydrin, which gives similar coloured spots.

questions.stem: In the mass spectrum of an organic compound, the molecular ion peak:
options: has the lowest m/z and shows the smallest fragment
shows the number of hydrogen atoms in the molecule
has the highest m/z of the main peaks and gives the molar mass
is always the tallest peak, and is assigned 100%
questions.explanation: The molecular ion, M⁺, is the whole molecule with one electron removed, so its m/z equals the molar mass. The tallest peak is the base peak, which is often a fragment rather than the molecular ion.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of propanone, CH₃COCH₃ (M = 58), has its base peak at m/z 43. Which ion causes this peak?
options: C₃H₇⁺, formed by loss of an oxygen atom
CH₃CO⁺, formed by loss of a CH₃ group
C₂H₅⁺, formed by loss of a CHO group
CH₃⁺, formed by loss of a CH₃CO group
questions.explanation: 58 − 43 = 15, the mass of a CH₃ group, so the molecular ion has lost a methyl group to leave CH₃CO⁺. C₃H₇⁺ also has m/z 43, but propanone has only six hydrogen atoms, so it cannot form this ion.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of chloroethane, C₂H₅Cl, shows molecular ion peaks at m/z 64 and 66 in a 3:1 ratio. What causes this?
options: Two different structural isomers of chloroethane
Loss of a methyl group from some molecules
The two isotopes, chlorine-35 and chlorine-37
Loss of two hydrogen atoms from some molecules
questions.explanation: Chlorine occurs naturally as about three parts chlorine-35 to one part chlorine-37, so molecules containing one Cl atom give two molecular ion peaks 2 units apart in about a 3:1 ratio.

questions.stem: A compound has a molecular ion at m/z 74. Its IR spectrum has a very broad absorption from 2500 to 3300 cm⁻¹ and a strong absorption at 1710 cm⁻¹. Which compound is it?
options: Butan-1-ol
Methyl ethanoate
Butanal
Propanoic acid
questions.explanation: A very broad 2500-3300 cm⁻¹ band is O-H in a carboxylic acid, and the 1710 cm⁻¹ band is C=O; propanoic acid, C₃H₆O₂, has M = 74. Butan-1-ol (also 74) has no C=O, methyl ethanoate (74) has no O-H, and butanal has M = 72.

questions.stem: Analysis shows an organic compound is 54.5% C, 9.1% H and 36.4% O by mass, and its molecular ion is at m/z 88. What is its molecular formula?
options: C₄H₈O₂
C₂H₄O
C₅H₁₂O
C₃H₄O₃
questions.explanation: Dividing by atomic masses gives C 4.54, H 9.03, O 2.28 mol, a ratio of 2:4:1, so the empirical formula is C₂H₄O (44 g/mol). 88/44 = 2, so the molecular formula is C₄H₈O₂. C₅H₁₂O also has a molar mass of 88 but does not fit the percentages.

questions.stem: What is the main use of the fingerprint region (below about 1500 cm⁻¹) of an IR spectrum?
options: Identifying the O-H group, which absorbs only in this region of the spectrum
Matching the whole pattern to a reference spectrum to confirm the compound's identity
Finding the molar mass of the compound from the position of the largest peak
Counting the hydrogen atoms in the compound from the number of peaks present
questions.explanation: The fingerprint region contains many overlapping absorptions that are unique to each compound, so it is compared with reference spectra. The O-H absorption is above 2500 cm⁻¹, and molar mass comes from mass spectrometry.

questions.stem: Fats that are solid at room temperature are usually rich in saturated fatty acids. Why?
options: Saturated chains are bent, so they tangle together and cannot flow
Saturated chains form hydrogen bonds with each other along their length
Saturated chains are straight, so they pack closely with strong dispersion forces
Saturated chains contain C=C bonds that form cross-links between molecules
questions.explanation: Triglycerides are esters of glycerol and fatty acids. Saturated chains have only single C-C bonds and can pack closely, giving stronger dispersion forces and higher melting points. cis C=C bonds in unsaturated chains create kinks that prevent close packing, so oils are liquid.

questions.stem: Organochlorine insecticides such as DDT persist and bioaccumulate in food chains. Which pair of properties explains this?
options: They are chemically unreactive and dissolve in fats rather than in water
They are very reactive and dissolve in water rather than in fats
They break down quickly and are excreted rapidly in urine
They are volatile gases that spread evenly through the air
questions.explanation: The stable C-Cl bonds make these compounds unreactive, so they break down very slowly in the environment. They are non-polar and fat-soluble, so they build up in fatty tissue and become more concentrated at each level of a food chain.
